scope.b_deferral_reason: The issue directs coordination with UTV2-1547's pm-decision/v1 schema rather than creating a second incompatible one. That schema has not landed, so implementing B here would either duplicate or pre-empt it. Original fixture 2 (a PM correction consumed on resume) is therefore not claimed.
b_seam: codex-exec.ts composes the resume brief at a single point before the spawn (readCheckpoint -> buildResumeBrief -> buildCodexPrompt(packet, resumeBrief)); buildCodexPrompt takes the brief as a parameter, so an amendment brief is a second argument at the same call site.

ExecutionCheckpoint is a versioned additive record (schema_version 1) that already persists per-attempt provenance; consumed amendment ids and updated_at values are a new field alongside findings/pending_actions, with no change to the resume path.

failVisiblyAndRelease is already the single fail-closed exit that closes the attempt and releases held resources; 'conflicting authoritative amendments stop before code' is a new outcome routed through it, not new machinery.
Every attempt already emits a structured `execution` block on stdout and closes with a recorded outcome; an amendment acknowledgement is another field on that block.
scope.b_deliberately_absent: No notion of authoritative comment authors, no precedence rule between description and amendments, and no comment parsing. Those are the decisions UTV2-1547 owns.

self_review.summary: Reviewing this lane's own diff before certifying it surfaced three ways the same failure class could have survived inside the fix itself. Both were fixed and checked in both directions.

findings.gap: readSemaphoreStatus and reapVerifySlots iterated `slot < maxConcurrent`, so lowering UNIT_TALK_FULL_VERIFY_CONCURRENCY from 2 to 1 left a corpse in slot-1 that nothing would ever inspect again -- never listed, never reclaimed.
findings.why_it_matters: That is 'a dead owner holds something forever', relocated inside the fix.
findings.fix: Both functions now scan the configured range union any slot-N directory actually present on disk.

findings.gap: release() used `if (current && current.operation_id !== operationId) return;`, so a MISSING record fell through to the delete. The one window in which the record can be missing is between another process's mkdirSync(slotPath) and its own record write.
findings.why_it_matters: That path could drop a slot out from under a verify that was starting at that instant -- the exact invariant this lane exists to protect.
findings.fix: Release now requires positive ownership (`current?.operation_id !== operationId`). A directory orphaned by this branch classifies as corrupt_orphan past the write grace and is reclaimed normally, so it is not a leak.

findings.gap: beginAttempt appended a new attempt without closing any prior one, and classifyCheckpointLiveness took the FIRST open attempt. A codex-exec killed before it could call finishAttempt left a dangling open record, and the next run's liveness check described that stale attempt instead of the run in flight.
findings.why_it_matters: The lane exists because long-running work loses progress when stopped abruptly; this session was itself stopped abruptly mid-implementation, and the defect it exposed in this lane's own code was the same shape as the defect the lane was opened to fix.
findings.fix: beginAttempt closes any dangling attempt as silent_no_heartbeat -- the failure it actually was, never success -- and liveness takes the LAST open attempt. Progress recorded by the killed attempt is still carried forward.

both_directions.method: The four new assertions were run against the pre-fix implementation and then against the fixed one.

fail: 37 a slot above the configured concurrency is still reported, not orphaned forever
38 a dead slot above the configured concurrency is reclaimed rather than leaked
40 release requires positive ownership: a slot mid-acquire by someone else is left alone
22 an attempt left open by a killed runner is closed as silence when the next attempt starts
23 liveness describes the attempt in flight, not an older dangling one
pass: 39 a LIVE slot above the configured concurrency is still not reclaimed

both_directions.honest_note: Assertion 39 passes in both directions BY CONSTRUCTION and is not counted as a regression test: pre-fix the slot was not scanned at all, so nothing was reaped either. It exists to stop the widened scan from widening what may be REAPED -- a guard against the fix over-reaching, which is the specific way this change could have hurt a live verifier.

implementation_runtime_evidence.note: This lane's own implementation (sections A and C: resumable execution, crash-safe verify semaphore) has no database surface -- it is OS-process-level logic (signals, /proc probes, timers). This key preserves the ORIGINAL runtime evidence for this lane's actual implementation -- the live OS-process fixture demonstrations -- which `ops:proof-repair apply` replaced when it wrote the new `runtime_proof` block, per its own documented behavior of owning that key wholesale. Restored here rather than left lost, since verification.md's prose already carries the full narrative and this key keeps evidence.json's machine-readable copy in sync with it.

fixtures.name: a dead process holding a full-verify slot is safely reaped and the next waiter admitted
fixtures.method: A real holder process acquired slot 0, then was SIGKILLed so no cleanup handler could run. The operator command was then run against the surviving record, and a second holder acquired.

observed.before_kill: slot 0: LIVE, owner pid=95675, reason 'owner pid 95675 is running and heartbeating'
observed.after_kill: slot 0: DEAD_OWNER (reapable), reason 'owner pid 95675 is not running on this host.'
observed.audit_record: reap-log.jsonl recorded state dead_owner, the reason, the reclaiming pid/operation_id, and the full previous owner record

fixtures.unit_assertion: FIXTURE: a dead process holding a slot is safely reaped and the next waiter admitted

fixtures.name: a live slow verifier is NOT reaped
fixtures.method: With the second holder still running, `ops:verify-slots reap` was invoked. The heartbeat was then sampled twice, three seconds apart, while the owner was idle in its event loop.

observed.protection_stated: protected slot 0: live -- owner pid 96707 is running and heartbeating (lease until 2026-07-31T12:50:17.654Z).

unit_assertions: FIXTURE: a live slow verifier is never reaped, however long it has been running (5.5h of work, still live, reapable false)
a live owner whose heartbeat merely lapsed is reported, not reaped (live_heartbeat_stale, reapable false)
a live owner past its lease is reported but still not auto-reaped (expired_live_owner, reapable false)
a foreign-host owner is protected until its lease expires (live_foreign_host, reapable false)
FIXTURE: a live slow verifier is not reaped and a contender queues behind it (holder operation_id and pid unchanged; reap-log.jsonl never created)
the heartbeat keeps beating while the main thread is blocked in spawnSync

fixtures.name: a recycled pid is not mistaken for a live owner
fixtures.method: /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 (starttime) is fixed for the life of a process. Rather than wait for the kernel to wrap the pid space, the record's process_start_token was rewritten while the pid stayed alive -- the exact state a recycled pid produces.

observed.reason: pid 96707 is running but is a different process than the slot owner (recorded start linux:starttime:1, current start linux:starttime:59319); the pid was recycled.
observed.note: A bare process.kill(pid, 0) liveness check would have reported this slot as live indefinitely. The reap removed the slot, not the process.

unit_assertions: a recycled pid is detected and is not mistaken for a live owner
a matching start token keeps a live owner protected
readProcessStartToken is stable for a live process and absent for a dead pid
readProcessStartToken distinguishes two different live processes
bootIdsProveReboot only fires when both sides are real kernel boot ids

fixtures.name: signal, crash and expiry cleanup
fixtures.method: Real child processes spawned as `node <script>` (no wrapper that could swallow a signal), one terminated with SIGTERM and one allowed to throw.
unit_assertions: a killed process releases its slot through the signal path
an uncaught exception releases the slot before the process dies (slot released, exit still non-zero, original error still on stderr)
installVerifySlotReleaseHandlers can be uninstalled and leaves no listeners behind
release does not delete a slot that has since been re-claimed by someone else
the hard deadline retires even a live, heartbeating owner
an incomplete slot is protected inside the write grace and reapable after it

fixtures.unit_assertion: FIXTURE: four consecutive timeout/resume attempts become one resumable history, not four replays
